subject: Azure private-offer: consolidated pricing + channel pass-through
messages:
From: Nora Blake <nora.blake@nimbus.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Nimbus Analytics Sales <sales@nimbus.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Azure private offer + channel pass-through

Hi Vivek,

Quick ask as we prep our FY28 cloud commitments: can Redwood provide a consolidated private-offer structure on Azure that supports staged list-price discounts (a pricing "staircase") tied to commit buckets, and also a clear pass-back/commission to our reseller (CloudBridge)? They need to see:

- list price tiers and effective net price per tier
- recommended channel margin (what Redwood pays to CloudBridge per tier)
- a diagram of how Azure private-offer credits flow to reseller (pass-through)
- any constraints around SKU bundling or usage thresholds that would change the price

We are the lead contact on this deal (Deal ID: DEAL-2027-089). Target decision window is Aug 16.

Thanks — can you send a consolidated sheet and a short note on implementation (billing + invoicing cadence)?

Best,
Nora
Nora Blake
Head of Strategic Procurement, Nimbus Analytics
On behalf of the Nimbus deal team

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Nora Blake <nora.blake@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Nimbus Analytics Sales <sales@nimbus.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Azure private offer + channel pass-through

Hi Nora — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a consolidated pricing staircase (xlsx) and a passback flow diagram (pdf). High level:

- Proposal: 3-tier staircase by committed ARR on Azure private offer (0-1M / 1-5M / 5M+) with escalating list discounts (5% / 12% / 20%).
- Channel margin to CloudBridge (recommended): 8% / 6% / 4% of list price per tier (we model a decreasing pass-through as scale improves net economics).
- Effective net price = list price * (1 - list_discount) - channel_margin (note channel margin is paid from Redwood's margin).

Implementation notes (short):
- Azure private offer will be issued at list price; discounts applied via private-offer price adjustments and invoiced monthly on committed consumption.
- CloudBridge will be set up as a partner passback via the marketplace private-offer pass-through agreement; we will provide the PO terms template for your procurement team.
- Attachments: azure_pricing_staircase_v1.xlsx (breakdown), channel_passback_flow.pdf (ops diagram), PO-Terms-Template.docx.

If you want, I can run a quick run-rate model with your expected usage mix to show net economics for each tier — send a rough SKU/usage split and I’ll drop the numbers.

Next step: I’ll loop in our channel ops (Vanessa) to validate passback flow and finalize legal wording.

Best,
Vivek
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | redwood.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: FYI: markup on Nimbus proposal (internal)

Vivek / team — I reviewed the attached staircase. A few internal notes before we finalize to customer:

- Channel margin: if we pay a flat % to CloudBridge from our side, we need to model both (1) the expense (to Redwood P&L) and (2) the operational passback mechanism (partner invoice vs. marketplace settlement). For Azure, marketplace settlement latency ~45 days is typical.
- Suggested modification to proposals: convert the top-tier passback to a volume-based rebate instead of a flat per-month margin. This reduces near-term cash outflow.
- Bundling caveat: if customer mixes high-memory GPU SKU consumption, we should exclude those from the standard staircase and treat as add-on premium (we take 7% higher list multiplier).

Ben / Aditya — can you run two scenarios in the xlsx: (A) flat % pass-through per month, (B) annual volume rebate paid at reconciliation? Need OPEX/cashflow delta.

Vanessa
Senior Manager, Channel Ops

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 13:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FYI: markup on Nimbus proposal (internal)

On Tue, Aug 10, 2027 at 11:02 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
> Ben / Aditya — can you run two scenarios in the xlsx: (A) flat % pass-through per month, (B) annual volume rebate paid at reconciliation? Need OPEX/cashflow delta.

Attached updated sheet with both scenarios sketched out. Quick takeaways:
- Scenario A (monthly pass-through): simulates steady partner cashflow but increases short-term cash outflow by ~1.8% of committed ARR in year 1 due to timing differences.
- Scenario B (annual rebate): Redwood retains cash in-year; partner receives a lump sum at reconciliation. Operational complexity rises slightly (annual reconciliation).

I also added a sample clause for the PO-Terms-Template: "Partner pass-through payments may be structured as monthly settlements through Azure marketplace or as annual reconciliations invoiced by the partner upon meeting committed thresholds."

Ben
Senior Commercial Analyst

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Nora Blake <nora.blake@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Nimbus Analytics Sales <sales@nimbus.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure private-offer: consolidated pricing + channel pass-through

Hi Nora — thanks for the patience. Quick summary and ask:

- Attached: revised staircase (v1.1) reflecting two settlement options (monthly pass-through vs annual rebate) and the effective net price table per tier. See the "ops notes" tab for the passback flow we intend to use.
- We recommend the annual rebate model for Nimbus given your preference to avoid monthly settlement volatility; CloudBridge signaled they prefer predictable reconciliation as well.
- Action items: please confirm (A) preferred settlement model (monthly vs annual), and (B) whether high-memory GPU SKUs should be excluded from the staircase and priced as separate add-ons.

If you confirm, we will prepare the private-offer draft and DocuSign package (I’ll send the link once legal signs off on the final PO terms).

Best,
Vivek

From: Nora Blake <nora.blake@nimbus.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Nimbus Analytics Sales <sales@nimbus.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure private-offer: consolidated pricing + channel pass-through

Vivek — this looks good, thanks. Nimbus confirms: annual rebate model, and exclude high-memory GPU SKUs from the staircase (we will treat them as a 7% premium add-on).

Please proceed with private-offer draft and send the DocuSign link. Our procurement has the Deal ID and will standby for the PO.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Regards,
Nora
